speaker_notes: At the 80-watt USB-C operating point, the input readings gave a power factor of 0.99 and current THD of 3.98 percent. The blue bars show the individual input-current harmonics, and the orange curve shows the IEC 61000-3-2 Class A limits for each harmonic order. The vertical scale is logarithmic. The shown harmonic components are below the Class A limits at this point. Class A is the reference used for this general-purpose supply. The standard limits each harmonic current; power factor and THD summarize input quality. The 3.98 percent is the logged screen value; the harmonic table from a separate capture gives 4.53 percent when reconstructed. This comparison covers one operating point, rather than a full IEC test. The charge pump shapes the average input-current envelope, while variation in burst density over the line cycle can change its shape.

facts: The original graph is embedded without pixel edits; its blue harmonic bars lie below the plotted orange Class A limits for the shown 80 W point.
IEC limits refer to individual harmonic currents. Comparison of one operating point does not establish full IEC test conformity.
The logged 3.98% THD and 4.53% harmonic-table reconstruction come from separate records and the discrepancy is unresolved.
The charge-pump envelope and burst-density explanation is a mechanism, not an isolated diagnosis of the measured spectrum.
